section: 4. Winkelmann: The Truth of an Ancient Murder
description: The discovery that the father of archaeology, Winkelmann, was murdered as early as 1768. A successful dice check uncovered this 155-year-old cold case, making the client's motive for seeking a long-dead person increasingly suspicious.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: player4 observes the family portraits: in the oldest frame is a man in Renaissance crimson velvet robes, the Victorian era features an elegant woman, and the most recent oil painting shows an elderly gentleman in a suit stroking a Persian cat.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Antonio walks towards the coffee cabinet, his left sleeve swaying slightly with the movement. Only then do you notice that his left cuff is meticulously sewn shut with black silk thread—it appears to be a missing arm. Antonio then steadily tilts the silver coffee pot with his right hand, pouring dark brown liquid into porcelain cups bearing the family crest.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Sir, this might be somewhat impertinent, but your hand...?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Antonio's right hand strokes the empty sleeve. The 1917 Isonzo campaign—an old story from the Austro-Hungarian 94th Infantry Regiment. Shrapnel took my left arm, but left me with these.

conversation.text: #observe the old professor's expression; his story about the left arm might not be false, but whether it's complete we cannot know.

conversation.text: The Bora turns the streets into roaring tunnels, gravel and ice pellets lash against building exteriors with gunshot-like cracks. Several local pedestrians are hunched over, struggling forward, their hands gripping the cast-iron chains running down the center of the street, their clothes flapping like desperate flags in the wind. The chains hum and vibrate in the gale. A short, stout man's felt hat is snatched by the wind, disappearing instantly into the gray mist. The stray cat in player4's arms lets out a sharp cry, its claws hooking onto his shirt buttons.

The Fascist fasces emblem on the other's collar insignia is almost pressed against player4's nose. The smell of tobacco and hair oil mixes with spittle spraying onto his face. The stray cat darts out from the torn pocket, its claws leaving white scratches on the Blackshirt's riding boots.

conversation.speaker: player4

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The investigators follow a lane planted with laurel trees to a cream-colored apartment building, brass nameplate gleaming faintly under the gas lamp. The butler silently leads them through a foyer piled with ancient books. Montanelli's study looks as if swept by a knowledge storm—an opened Byzantine Empire codex lies askew on the Persian rug, a plaster statue balances a draft of an ink-stained thesis on its head. Montanelli nods from behind the book piles, a wool blanket neatly spread over his lap on the wheelchair. Antonio just called, he pushes his gold-rimmed glasses up the bridge of his nose, I heard you brought that Ancient Greek manuscript? The butler silently retreats outside the door.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Yes, that's right, sir." "Is your health not well?" #Simply observe the wheelchair. .ra Spot Hidden

conversation.speaker: player5

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Among the piled books lie ordinary academic items: a gilded globe marked with ancient trade routes, a brass microscope beside marine life sketches. The stray cat squirms uneasily in his arms, but there are no objects related to sacrifice in the room. No, normal vomit. Montanelli adjusts the wheelchair angle, Joseph the butler and I live here making a living from translation—German contracts, Slovenian shipping documents, things like that. He points to the scattered papers on the desk, occasionally getting ancient Latin documents from the Vatican is what's interesting. If the new university really gets started next year, maybe I can even teach Ancient Greek conjugation.

conversation.speaker: player4

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Montanelli puts on a magnifying glass to examine the paper, this variant mixed with Linear B... will take at least thirty-six hours—and hoping these old bones don't fall apart in the meantime. The butler silently brings a coffee pot. "Come find me for the translation the morning after tomorrow."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Alright, thank you, Professor." "Then if there's nothing else, we'll take our leave."
